newsitem.title: USA: Traders see explosive CBOT Dec corn, meal expiry. [CORRECTED 23:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Traders see explosive CBOT Dec corn, meal expiry. [CORRECTED 23:36 GMT]

text.p: Large open interest numbers in Chicago Board of Trade December corn and soybean meal futures could spark explosive gains ahead of the contract expiry at 1201 CST/1801 GMT Thursday, analysts and traders said.
"Funds are still short the December (corn) and are getting out," a floor trader said. "It (expiration) could be explosive and I think we'll be higher for the next several days."
CBOT pegged preliminary corn open interest at 22.5 million bushels as of Dec 17, down 12.8 million from the previous day.
Soymeal open interest stood at 3,120 lots, down 1,668 from the previous day, according to CBOT data.
At 1215 CST Wednesday, CBOT December corn futures were 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher at $2.76-1/2 and soymeal was $4.00 per ton higher at $245.00 a ton.

"We still have a pretty good amount of corn and soymeal open interest," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with The Chicago Corporation. "We took a nice bite out of both of them yesterday but they're still pretty good numbers."
Armstrong said open interest in corn needed to fall by 12 million to 15 million bushels on Wednesday to assure the market of a quiet expiry.

"If we took out only eight (million in corn) that would make the market a little nervous," he said. "In soymeal, we had 3,120 lots this morning. That needs to at least halve today and you'd really like to see it get under 1,000 lots. The shorts are in trouble in meal."
Cash basis levels remained firm for corn and soymeal and no deliveries were posted against the December, supporting ideas that demand for corn and meal was strong.
"We've been trading at very high premiums for spot meal," said Nick DeBrown, analyst and trader with NX Analytics. "I get the feeling there's more to the export side than people are saying."
DeBrown and others speculated funds were short December corn while some commercials were believed to be holding positions in December soymeal.

As of December 3, non-commercial accounts including funds were short corn (all contracts) by 279.2 million bushels and long 52.9 million bushels, according to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

CFTC said commercial accounts were short soymeal by 56,994 (corrects from 60.8 million tonnes) contracts (of 100 tons each) and long by 60.8 million tonnes (corrects from 'short by 44.1 million tonnes') as of Dec 3.
Three firms with commercial ties were noted spreaders of the January/December soymeal on Tuesday which supported ideas commercials were rolling out of short positions, traders said.
Pit sources said Goldenberg-Hehmeyer spread 400 lots while Refco spread 300 and Smith Barney spread 200. Cargill was said to be an outright buyer of December soymeal.
